rationale: This qualitative study (38 semi-structured interviews, participant observation, participatory mapping, and a focus group with Lilongwe Water Board staff) examines how uncodified street-level bureaucratic discretion, ad hoc valve manipulation, case-by-case backup-line diversions, high-pressure bypass connections for influential clients, and differentiated maintenance responses by utility engineers and operators (`discretion_accommodation`) produce socio-spatial inequalities in water supply continuity, pressure, and service hours across low-income versus high-income areas within Lilongwe's piped network (`effective_access`).
